input: Sew a patchwork quilt from old band T-shirts

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of T-shirts and the intended quilt size directly determines the cutting layout, number of patches, and how much additional fabric or batting is needed.
Whether the quilt is for personal use, a gift, or a memorial piece changes the emotional weight of decisions like arrangement, personalisation, and finishing quality.
Sewing skill level determines whether the plan should include beginner-friendly steps, special techniques for stretchy jersey fabric, or assume prior quilting experience.
Access to a sewing machine versus hand-sewing, and ownership of tools like rotary cutters, quilting rulers, or an iron, shapes which methods and steps are practical.
The desired quilt pattern (simple grid, diagonal, irregular mosaic, etc.) and whether to include sashing or borders significantly changes the cutting and assembly plan.
The intended use of the quilt — display on a wall, use on a bed, or a lap throw — determines the required finished dimensions and durability of construction.
Knowing whether the priority is preserving every graphic intact, achieving a heirloom-quality finish, or simply completing a functional quilt quickly guides trade-off decisions throughout.

gold.taskTitle: Sew a patchwork quilt from band T-shirts
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to create a patchwork quilt using old band T-shirts as the fabric source.

questions.title: How many T-shirts do you have to work with?
questions.description: The number of shirts determines the quilt size that is achievable and how many additional fabric panels or filler squares will be needed.

questions.title: Who is this quilt being made for?
questions.description: Knowing the recipient — yourself, a partner, a child, or as a gift — shapes decisions about personalisation, sizing, and the care put into the finish.

questions.title: How would you describe your current sewing experience level?
questions.description: Skill level determines whether the plan needs to cover jersey-fabric handling basics, interfacing techniques, and beginner-friendly seam allowances, or can assume quilting knowledge.

questions.title: Do you have a sewing machine, or will you sew by hand?
questions.description: Available tools — sewing machine, rotary cutter, quilting ruler, iron — directly dictate which construction methods and steps are feasible.

questions.title: What block layout or pattern are you imagining for the quilt?
questions.description: The preferred pattern — uniform grid, diagonal set, varied block sizes, with or without sashing — changes how patches are cut and assembled.

questions.title: Will the quilt be used on a bed, as a lap throw, or hung on a wall?
questions.description: Intended use determines the target finished dimensions, batting thickness, and how robust the construction needs to be.

questions.title: Is preserving every graphic fully intact your top priority?
questions.description: Knowing whether the focus is on showcasing complete shirt graphics, achieving a polished heirloom finish, or simply getting a functional quilt done quickly guides key trade-off decisions.
